name: Chanterelle
habitat: Broadleaf and conifer forests, often near oak and beech
description: One of the most prized edible mushrooms in the world. Golden-yellow, funnel-shaped cap with forking false gills running down the stem. Fruity, apricot-like aroma.
identification_tips: Cap is golden to egg-yolk yellow, wavy and irregular
False gills: forked ridges, not true gills — they run down the stem
Stem is solid and the same colour as the cap

lookalikes.name: Jack-o'-lantern mushroom (Omphalotus olearius)
lookalikes.difference: Has true gills (not forking ridges), grows in clusters at the base of trees, glows faintly in the dark

safety_warning: Always confirm identification with an expert before consuming. Never eat a mushroom you are not 100% certain about.

name: Porcini
habitat: Conifer and broadleaf forests, often near pine, spruce, and oak
description: Known as the king of mushrooms. Large, brown cap with a thick white to brown stem covered in a fine net-like pattern. White flesh that does not change colour when cut.
identification_tips: Cap is brown, smooth and rounded like a bun
Pores underneath (not gills) — white when young, turning yellowish with age
Stem is thick and bulbous with a white net pattern
Flesh stays white when cut — does not blue or discolour

lookalikes.name: Satan's bolete (Rubroboletus satanas)
lookalikes.difference: Has red pores underneath the cap and the flesh turns blue immediately when cut

safety_warning: Always confirm identification with an expert before consuming. Never eat a mushroom you are not 100% certain about.

name: Fairy Ring Mushroom
habitat: Lawns, meadows, and grassy areas — often growing in rings or arcs
description: A small but tasty mushroom that grows in distinctive fairy rings on grass. Tan to buff cap that flattens with age. Tough, wiry stem. Dries well and keeps its flavour.
identification_tips: Grows in rings or arcs on grass or meadows
Cap is tan to buff, bell-shaped when young, flattening with age
Gills are widely spaced and do not run down the stem
Stem is very tough and wiry — hard to snap

lookalikes.name: Fool's funnel (Clitocybe rivulosa)
lookalikes.difference: Has crowded gills running down the stem and no tough wiry stem. Often grows alongside fairy ring mushrooms — be very careful.

safety_warning: Always confirm identification with an expert before consuming. Never eat a mushroom you are not 100% certain about.
